Happy Veterans Day!

This year’s commemoration is extra special in Moundsville, WV, because Raymond Carl Richmond is finally coming home.

Mr. Richmond served as a flight engineer aboard a B-29 Superfortress in WWII until his plane was shot down over Tokyo in April 1945. 

He was then captured and held as a POW, dying weeks later when fires from the bombing of Tokyo reached his prison.

After 81 years, his remains were identified this summer, and today he is returning to his family in Marshall County, where this year’s Veterans Day ceremony is dedicated to his memory.

May he rest in peace. May we never forget the sacrifices of those who served, and may we honor the families who have waited for them to come home.

12/ Our task for the next two years is to show hard working Americans that we’re the ones who really represent their interests and will advance the policies they want.

We must prioritize communities over corporations, American workers over cheap foreign labor, family health over profit margins, domestic flourishing over foreign entanglements and truly put Americans First.

11/ What should all this tell us?

To me it says that Americans want a populist, America First agenda, and they will reward whichever party they believe is ready to fight harder for it.

Right now, that’s the Democrats. The new Texas governor, Gina Hinojosa, and others are actively dropping the “progressive” label and calling themselves populists.

10/ Here are just a few examples:

- Bans on men in women’s sports passed in AZ, NE, CO, and WA

- Voter ID and Citizenship-to-Vote amendments passed in AL, AR, KS, NV, NC, OH, SD, and of course, WV

- Tax cuts or rejection of tax hikes passed in FL, IA, LA, NC, and TN https://t.co/jmCSmdwD9s

9/ All of this told the American people that our party wasn’t willing to do what was required to advance the policies we ran on.

As a result, many Americans split their tickets last week, supporting Republican policies and ballot measures while also voting for Democrat candidates.

8/ In fact, we did the opposite.

The one week we planned to vote on labor bills, what was on the floor?

A joint employer bill that labor opposed, and a bill letting employers exclude voluntary professional development and training activities from calculations for minimum wage and overtime.

7/ 2024 was a breakthrough for Republicans with the labor vote.

@TeamsterSOB became the first Teamsters president in 121 years to address the RNC.

Harris lost men in union households by 9 points. Biden had won them by 10 in 2020.

And yet, The House had zero plans to pass any legislation to help the American worker and give a nod to our new allies in labor.

6 / Congress took foreign policy restraint even less seriously.

Putting more scrutiny on foreign assistance and a clearer focus on the Western Hemisphere and our core national interests was a real priority for some of the leading figures in this administration.

But the 119th Congress wasn’t interested in advancing that approach. Instead, the neocons continued to dominate, even to the point of forcing a vote to continue funding the Ukraine War.

5/ Immigration is a similar story. 

President Trump secured the border, but Congress utterly failed to pass bills that reform our broken system or cut off the supply of cheap foreign labor. 

- @KenCalvert’s Legal Workforce Act (H.R. 251) would’ve made E-Verify permanent and mandatory for every employer.

- My Stop CCP VISAs Act (H.R. 2147) would’ve ended student visas for Chinese nationals. We hand out nearly 300,000 a year, and the CCP has used them to spy on our military and steal American research.

- @RepEliCrane’s End H-1B Visa Abuse Act (H.R. 8443) would’ve paused new H-1B visas for three years and totally transformed the program.

None of them even got out of committee.

4/ Consider MAHA, which was one of the most popular parts of the President’s ‘24 campaign.

- The Ban Harmful Food Dyes Act (H.R. 5027) was introduced in Aug. ‘25. It never got out of committee.

- The No Tricks on Treats Act (H.R. 5882), introduced Oct. ‘25, would’ve required labels to disclose dyes, flavorings and sweeteners. It never got out of committee.

- The House’s original Farm Bill included preemptive language giving pesticide and glyphosate companies liability protections. We had to fight tooth and nail to get a floor vote for the @RepLuna amendment, which stripped those provisions. It passed overwhelmingly (280-142), but it took an immense fight.

3/ Congressional Rs also took almost all of the most energetic parts of the victorious ‘24 coalition for granted.

- MAHA
- Immigration enforcement
- Foreign policy restrainers
- Labor

President Trump gave these groups influential positions in his cabinet, but Congressional Rs didn’t give them the time of day on Capitol Hill or work to pass legislation they cared about.

2/ You can see this clearly in the 13 Democrat-held districts Trump won in ‘24.

No one stopped to ask why the President outran Congressional Rs there, or what he offered that they didn’t.

Instead, many on our side simply chalked them up as easy ‘26 pickups.

That was wrong. https://t.co/A8wOwdvfJF

Again, our policies didn’t fail. Our party did.
